item.title: Why DMARC Enforcement Fails: Misconfiguration, Ignored Policies, and the Identity Problem
item.description: Email authentication protocols like DMARC suffer from practical friction and widespread misconfiguration. System administrators routinely ignore enforcement policies to avoid dropping legitimate email from misconfigured senders, while spammers easily pass authentication checks, leaving the fundamental problem of sender trust unsolved. Quote: The core problem is that the real need of email end users need is a way of determining whether or not to trust a given sender.
